title: M (1931) through the leans of fascism

commenti.body: It's an interesting point. Have you seen Lang's follow up to M, the Testament of Dr. Mabuse (1933). It also speaks quite directly to the rising fascism in Germany at the time. Lang was quite passionately against Nazis (though his wife at the time, Thea von Harbou was not), and many of his 40s films are very overtly anti-Nazi.

> united voice for execution of the killer is what is portrayed as the most sought-after outcome.

Just to make it explicit, they seem to represent democracy in that they are at least looking for some sort of consensus.

> He is evil and unsympathetic

Unsympathetic until that final speech where we, the audience, are forced to have sympathy even for him.  Not that he shouldn't be executed, but we must have compassion.  That's a pretty classically "liberal" view.

Thank you for taking the time to read! I believe this was the first film I’ve ever seen of Lang’s. I’m definitely interested in seeing more of his work, your recommendation above seems as good a place as any to start. 
I appreciate you providing some insight into his stance on fascism, because I honestly thought a case could be for being both anti-fascist or pro-fascist (the bit about his wife being pro-fascist is quite fascinating). When looking at it as an anti-fascist film, it suddenly to me, begins to feel almost like a political satire in a very clever guise — it really makes it all that much more brilliant.

Lang previously made Metropolis, which his wife wrote. They eventually split: his wife was an antisemite and Lang, half Jewish, renounced his German citizenship and moved to America. The horrors of World War I destabilized society. People's faith in humanity and belief in God were shaken; as Nietzsche said "God is Dead". His philosophy of master morality and the blond beast would be used by the Nazis. Lorre represents the role of the scapegoat in facism. But Metropolis shows how above all Facism is built on love and heroism. Hitler adored the film so much he was willing to look past Lang's Jewish heritage if Lang became a Nazi propagandist.

The Germans felt victimized by the treaty of Versailles, which gave the Germans about half a trillion dollars in today's money to pay in restitution for WWI. The ensuing hardships pushed Germans torward Communism and Nazism. But with the Reichstag Fire happened; it was probably caused by Nazis to frame the Communists and seize power. 

The apartment bombings in Russia are seen as Putin's Reichstag Fire. Putin saw the fall of the Soviet Union as "the greatest geopolitical catastrophe of the 20th century". Like Hitler, he promised to restore his, in his view humiliated and victimized country's greatness. Like a cry bully, he professed victim hood and claimed he was only doing what Ukraine would have done to Russia. He called them Nazis. Russia suffered roughly the same population loss as the Jews during WWII. But Stalin was responsible for the Ukrainian Holocaust, the Holodomor, which starved millions of Ukrainians through forced industrialization and collectivization. 

Nazi propagandist Goebbels said of Metropolis, "the political bourgeoisie is about to leave the stage of history. In its place advance the oppressed producers of the head and hand, the forces of Labor, to begin their historical mission". Lang went on to say he detested the film and thought it was a silly fairytale. Goebbels is thought to have said, "if you repeat a lie long enough, they'll believe it," and he thought the bigger the lie, the more likely it would be believed. 

Peter Lorre's character is probably insane and suffering from shellshock. Scapegoats don't have to be guilty, but they can also be guilty. The mob has a show trial that's just a glorified lynching. Fascists rally around protecting children to garner support. Conspiracy theories like Pizzagate and drinking the blood of children echo Nazi propaganda. But after almost 100 years, M can be seen through the lens of authoritarianism, not just Facism. There's the theory that the further right or left you go, people are more likely to mirror each other; the boomerang theory doesn't hold true universally; the middle isn't necessarily correct and the Overton window shows how centrism can shift wildly. 

Speaking from personal experience, there are plenty of cry bullies who see themselves as victims or protectors of victims, when in reality they're just bullies looking for an easy target - marginalized groups like gays and the mentally ill, both of which I belong. In Nazi Germany I'd be considered a dead end and sent to the camps. While it's certainly true that the mentally ill can be violent, they're more likely to be victims of violence and the majority of violence is committed by those without any diagnosable mental disorder. In Christian philosophy, Jesus said what you do to the least of these you do to me. The child killer is the least human of all. But he's insane. The mob doesn't have that excuse. They put their inhumanity against his and feel just great in comparison. Today if someone, like me, is rumored to be a predator (I am not; I'd never want to hurt anyone; I have a clear record), the whole community bonds over their hatred : cryptofacists and keyboard activists get to play what psychiatrist Eric Berne described as the most common game, Ain't it Awful. 

> First they came for the socialists, and I did not speak out—because I was not a socialist.

>Then they came for the trade unionists, and I did not speak out—because I was not a trade unionist.

>Then they came for the Jews, and I did not speak out—because I was not a Jew.

>Then they came for me—and there was no one left to speak for me.

>—Martin Niemöller

Weimar era Germany was bustling with ideas. Dadaism, Surrealism, and Expressionism were a reaction against the rigidity of groupthink and Facism. Most people doubted a catastrophe was coming. WWI was deemed the war to end all wars. But WWII was far bloodier. To suggest the world may be on the verge of world war 3 or America is on the verge of becoming a dictatorship would be met with guffaws from people who think you have Cassandra symptom. Historian Timothy Snyder gave his number one rule to combat and prevent Facism - don't obey in advance. 

> If only it were all so simple! If only there were evil people somewhere insidiously committing evil deeds, and it were necessary only to separate them from the rest of us and destroy them. But the line dividing good and evil cuts through the heart of every human being. And who is willing to destroy a piece of his own heart? - Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn

You should definitely seek out the Kino restoration of Metropolis. It has 25 minutes of footage previously thought lost. I also suggest The Big Heat if you like film noir. His silent film Destiny is an overlooked horror parable. If you like the Grimm brothers you'd probably like this. I haven't seen Die Nibelungen or Dr Mabuse, which are considered masterpieces.
Nietzsche’s quote of god being dead has nothing to do with World War 1, as he died in 1900.

I just meant the phrase had new meaning; the deaths must have put strain on religious belief for some. I assumed a lot of people lost faith in their religion because of the war, but I can't find any evidence of that.
